recipes.name: Fish Fillets Italiano
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup black olives, pitted and sliced

steps.text: In a large frying pan, heat oil over medium heat. Saute onions and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Stir in tomatoes, olives, parsley, and wine. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Place fillets in sauce. Simmer for about 5 more minutes, or until fish turns white.

raw_recipe.headline: Fish Fillets Italiano
raw_recipe.description: Cod and haddock fillets work well for this braised dish. An extra easy and quick way to fix a superb tasting fish dish! Serve over rice.

review.reviewBody: This is a five star recipe -- with the following changes: add 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, and italian seasoning. I actually added 2 tsp italian seasoning and 1 tsp pizza seasoning, as we like lots of seasoning. Since we have a toddler, we also chopped the onion fine and processed the tomatoes into smaller bits...she ate it up. Served over brown rice. We all agreed, it was delicious!

5 stars, with changes I made, many suggested by other reviewers. Added fresh herbs to the onion/garlic/tomato mixture: 1 Tbsp parsley, 1 Tbsp basil, 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp oregano; salt and pepper, and 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes. Used one 15 oz can of chicken broth, plus 2 Tbsp cooking sherry, instead of white wine. Simmered this mixture for about 40 minutes to thicken and blend flavors, then refrigerated until my guests arrived a couple of hours later, and then put the tomato mixture back on the stove. I seasoned the 4 cod filets on one side only with salt and 1/4 tsp dried oregano, and seasoned 1/2 lb raw shrimp with 1/4 tsp EVOO, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp dried oregano. I placed the cod in the pan and nestled it into the tomato mixture, and simmered, covered, about 5 minutes. Then I added the shrimp and cooked until opaque. Served over jasmine rice, with a side of corn on the cob. Very Easy, and Absolutely Delicious!

This recipe is a good base, but it needs tweaks to be flavourful. I used more garlic and parsley, chicken bouillon cube + water instead of the wine (didn't have any, but would definitely use it next time) and basa fillets instead of the cod (they were on sale). The result was relatively bland and soup-y, so I dissolved some cornstarch in water to make a paste to help thicken the dish. I also added about half a cup of Parmesan cheese and some Italian seasoning. I also used about two teaspoons of sweet bell pepper paste to get some of the red colour back (cornstarch and parm made the sauce very light coloured). This could definitely use a little heat as well. I would reduce some of the liquid next time (maybe use only some of the liquid from the diced tomatoes). Served this with 'Company Couscous' from AR.

Making it now... Based on other reviews, I tweeked it a bit by adding about 1/2 tsp Oregano, 1/2 tsp Basil, 1 Tbsp Capers, and 1/4 tsp Red Pepper flakes. No salt needed. Also, didn't have diced tomatoes so using crushed tomatoes - results in a smoother sauce. Using cod and serving over Polenta with a side of lightly steamed broccoli. Delicious!

Nice dish, I used fresh tomatoes, to make it. Since the recipe didn’t really have any seasoning I used a tablespoon of Italian seasoning as some others stated in reviews. I also used a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice in the sauce to brighten it up and put lemon wedges on the table. This is a very easy recipe to make your own! Thank you!!!

So easy and fast and delicious. Hubs loved this. I sprayed the pan with Pam instead of using olive oil. I omitted the olives (don't like them) and used a 10 oz can of Rotel tomatoes as that is what I had. I added about 1/4 cup tomato paste to make up for the tomatoes I didn't have. Since other reviews mention a bland flavor I went ahead and added a packet of Good Sense Italian dressing mix along with dried parsley. Used chicken broth instead of wine and sprinkled parmesean cheese over each serving. It actually turned out a bit spicy for the kids- the Rotel did it I think- but the adults thought it was awesome. Used cod that I mostly thawed in cold water 1st and they took about 10 minutes in the simmering sauce.

Outstanding recipe...so healthy too! Added dried basil and oregano and more olives and allowed the "sauce" to simmer for more time before adding the cod/haddock. Once the fish is added, spoon sauce over the tops and DO NOT overcook! Delicious Mediterranean dish.

We loved this! I used tilapia instead of cod – any firm white fish would work. I used fresh basil rather than the parsley, because my tomatoes were already seasoned with garlic, oregano and basil. I made the sauce early in the afternoon. When it was almost done I thickened it with a water/cornstarch slurry – just enough to give it some body. When it had cooled somewhat, I covered and refrigerated it. Then at dinnertime, I just brought it to a simmer and popped in the fish. Dinner was on the table in a flash! Excellent flavor for so little effort, a repeater for sure!

I was skeptical about fish and Italian but this dish was really good. I changed a few things. I used tilapia instead of cod and I used 1/2 cup chicken stock instead of wine plus 1/8 cup of cooking white wine. I also doubled the garlic and sprinkled each piece of fish with garlic powder. I also used basil/oregano diced tomatoes for more flavor and I served this over angel hair pasta sprinkled with olive oil and fresh grated Parmesan. 
I would definitely make this dish again! My husband who does not tilapia, loved it!

I'm rating this for the recipe as written. I made the onion/tomato mixture using real Calamanta Olives instead of canned black olives and it was okay but still kind of bland so I added some chopped, fresh rosemary, more garlic, about 1 Tsp. of dried Italian Herbs, a cup of mushrooms, a roasted red pepper (from a jar) a few grindings of black pepper and a quick dash of cayenne pepper. I let the veggies and sauce simmer till the liquid was reduced before adding the fish. I served the fish and tomato mixture with Quinoa. With those changes, the flavor was much better and brought it to a 5 star status.

This dish was really fantastic. I had to use Pollock fillets because it's what I had on hand. I did take the suggestions of other users and infused some traditional Italian flavor with the addition of oregano and basil. I think this was a nice touch. Because it's the new year and I wanted to hit the ground running with this whole dieting thing, I decided not to serve it with rice but instead to add white beans and artichoke hearts and serve it as more of a stew. Garnish with a little Parmesan cheese and it's over the top. Thank you for this wonderful rustic Italian recipe!

We like spicy so this time based on some of the reviews, added few red pepper flakes, extra garlic, bit of dry oregano & basil. Had canned black beans to use up so took a chance to replace other carb with them which added just enough salt to make my fussy family very happy!
This dish is so good! Very simple to make, dinner is ready in minutes. No tweaking necessary.

This was pretty easy to make and was very good! I added the extra spices like recommended and used stock because I was out of wine. I served it over rice. Next time, I’m going to cook the sauce more, use wine and serve over pasta. I can’t wait to make it again next week and explore different ingredients to add.

We loved this dish! I made this recipe using fresh tilapia from Costco. I used dried parsley and chicken broth in place of the white wine. I also had to simmer for 10 minutes for my large fillets to be done. We added salt and pepper to our desired taste at the table. I will be making this easy dish again!
I added more Italian seasoning, used green olives and added marinated artichoke hearts.

I've made this as written in the skillet and also in baked in oven. If you like more seasoning just add what you like. I do like to add a topping of buttered crumbs and parm in the oven. The olives make this delicious, green or black. I've gone Italian, Mexican or Mediterranean. If you find it bland you didn't use enough spice. Try it, you'll love it!
